newsitem.title: JAPAN: Early Asia oil sags, IOC buys four Dubai.
newsitem.headline: Early Asia oil sags, IOC buys four Dubai.

text.p: Crude prices in early Asia on Friday suffered the same OPEC-inspired volatility as Western markets, with cash Brent values quickly shedding 24 cents of the 34 cents gained a day earlier.
The skittishness grew out of trader skepticism that OPEC would hold true to claims that it would more closely scrutinize individual country production quotas.
Notional assessments for August cash Brent fell to $17.86/17.96 per barrel, down from Thursday levels of $18.10/18.20.
Asia physical markets were fresh with expectations of new Qatar and Oman deals this afternoon.
Earlier in the day, a Qatar Marine was heard sold from a French major to a U.S. major at an option of OSP minus 50 cts or even Dubai, whichever was cheaper, traders said.
In tender talks, state-owned India Oil Corp (IOC) awarded four Duabi cargoes, a 900,000 barrel parcel of Gulf of Suez, and one VLCC of Qua Iboe in its August buying crude tender, traders said.

Traders said the IOC awarded one cargo of Dubai to Spanish Repsol at first half quotes minus seven cents, one Dubai to Conoco at minus five cents, and two Dubai cargoes to Statoil at minus six and minus seven cents.
Glencore was heard to have been awarded a 900,000 barrel parcel of Gulf of Suez at OSP plus 25 cents.
Mobil was awarded one VLCC of Qua Iboe, traders said, but no price was disclosed.
